sections.title: A steady place to make sense of what you are carrying
paragraphs: Hi, I’m Amanda. I’m a Registered Clinical Counsellor (license #29097) with the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors.

While my counselling work currently focuses on eating disorder recovery and disordered eating, including anorexia, bulimia, orthorexia, binge eating, and body image concerns, I also welcome clients who may be looking for support with anxiety, depression, life transitions, self-worth, and burnout.

Early on in my undergraduate degree, I had the pleasure of meeting people in eating disorder recovery. They shared their stories with me, describing the isolation and stigma they felt and the lack of resources available to help them in their recovery.

Hearing their stories, witnessing their resilience, and admiring their vulnerability inspired me to volunteer with a local non-profit, Looking Glass Foundation, to help increase access to mental health support for those in eating disorder recovery. I deeply cherished my time there, so I returned as a practicum student during my graduate program to deepen my skill set.

I view eating disorders and disordered eating as ways people may have learned to cope with overwhelming experiences in their lives. Through my work, I have found that eating disorders don't typically exist in a vacuum, meaning other factors in our lives impact our relationship to food and our bodies and vice verse.

Anxiety, depression, burnout, struggles with self-worth, trauma, interpersonal relationship challenges, and life transitions are some common experiences that can often contribute to, maintain, and intensify challenges with food and body image.

That’s why, when we work together, we’ll explore your relationship to food and your body, while also looking at other areas of your life that may be impacting your recovery. We will work to understand what the eating disorder/disordered eating may be helping you cope with, while developing new coping strategies and skills to help you turn towards the eating disorder or disordered eating less and build a life that feels more fulfilling and aligned with who you are.

sections.title: Therapeutic approach
paragraphs: Because I believe that no two healing journeys are the same, I meet clients where they are and honour their individual pace, needs, and capacity throughout the process.

Through a person-centred and culturally informed lens, I take an integrative approach in my counselling work that blends mind-body therapeutic approaches with a particular focus on attachment and the impact of early experiences on well-being. Together, we can explore the approaches and strategies that feel most supportive and aligned for you, tailoring counselling to your unique needs.

The therapeutic approaches I typically draw from include Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Compassion-Focused Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), mindfulness, and psychodynamic approaches.
